The changelog rates v1.19.1 as Recommended for validators, so mainnet validators may run either revision.

Between evm2 66687c18 and 35aa3280 the files arithmetic.rs, bitwise.rs, i256.rs, control.rs, memory.rs, crypto.rs, stack.rs, bytecode/analysis.rs, analysis/x86.rs and analysis/aarch64.rs are byte identical; host.rs changes the SSTORE skip_cold_load threshold from ColdStorageAdditionalCost to ColdStorageCost and system.rs refactors call gas accounting (EIP-8037 refund of new-account state gas).

Tempo ships aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu release binaries (tempoup maps arm64 Linux to that target) and a linux/arm64 container image, so a validator can run the NEON jump destination kernel and the non-x86 ruint paths. No public source names the CPU of any mainnet validator.

ruint 1.21.1 (crate sha256 a0de3fa9..., equal to the Cargo.lock checksum) selects code by target: algorithms/mod.rs lines 147-219 use _subborrow_u64 for every multi-limb comparison and subtraction on x86_64 and a borrowing_sub chain elsewhere; div/reciprocal.rs line 28 and div/small.rs lines 75-87 and 139-153 use the x86 div instruction for the reciprocal and single-limb division and the MG10 reciprocal with normalised division elsewhere. mul_mod, add_mod and the 2^256-1 fast path (modular.rs 33-160) have no target-specific code of their own.

cleared.check: L-879: ruint 1.21.1 as built for x86_64 against the same crate with every target_arch = "x86_64" branch in algorithms/mod.rs, div/reciprocal.rs and div/small.rs forced to the non-x86 code, both against num-bigint, for every U256 operation evm2 calls (mul_mod, add_mod, wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, lt, gt, eq, is_zero, shl, shr, wrapping_mul, wrapping_add, wrapping_sub, wrapping_pow), 30 million iterations with edge limbs, the modulus 2^256-1 on one sixteenth and the 1.21.0 fault shape on one quarter.
cleared.result: 0 mismatches on either build. The withdrawn ruint 1.21.0 gives a wrong mul_mod on 2,834,980 of the 7,500,000 fault-shaped cases, so the harness sees the fault. A validator on aarch64 therefore computes the same MULMOD at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 and :48, the same comparisons at :25 and :52 and the same DIV at :35, :62, :67 and :73 as the x86 endpoint, up to compiler code generation for the other target, which was not run.

cleared.check: ruint 1.21.1 add_mod fast path (modular.rs 33-50) and the mul_mod end-around carry for modulus 2^256-1 (modular.rs 119-127), read line by line.
cleared.result: Correct as read. The fast path requires both operand high limbs at most the modulus high limb, which bounds each operand below twice the modulus, and it handles the carry out of the sum. For modulus 2^256-1 the folded sum plus carry cannot overflow because a carry implies the sum is at most 2^256-2, and a result equal to the modulus is mapped to zero. These are the paths of mulmod(a, b, not(0)) at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24.

cleared.check: Does a validator still on tempo/v1.19.0 (evm2 66687c18) compute something different from the v1.19.1 endpoint (evm2 35aa3280) in any instruction the PoolManager uses?
cleared.result: No. The arithmetic, bitwise, signed, control, memory, keccak, stack and jump destination files are byte identical. host.rs moves the SSTORE threshold below which a cold slot is not loaded from 2,000 to 2,100 remaining gas after the 100 gas static charge; a cold SSTORE needs 2,100 more gas in both revisions, so both halt the frame out of gas in that window and differ only in whether the slot was loaded first. system.rs refactors call gas and refunds EIP-8037 new-account state gas to the caller's reservoir when a value-carrying call that would create its target fails; that changes the gas left, not the success flag or return data of the call.

leadResults.answer: T14 is not live until 2026-12-08 and no T15 release exists. Found this cycle: the T14-required tempo/v1.19.0 pins evm2 66687c18 and ruint 1.21.1, v1.19.1 pins evm2 35aa3280 and ruint 1.21.1, and the two revisions have identical arithmetic, bitwise, control, memory, stack and jump analysis files. 9,000 new edge vectors match under a T14 block time override. The live-fork rerun is carried forward as a new lead.

No T15 release is published (network upgrades page and T15 page, 2026-11-25; Cargo.lock at tempo/v1.19.2, v1.20.0 and rc tags returns 404). main still pins evm2 35aa3280 and ruint 1.21.1. Carried in the new high lead.

The T15 release does not exist yet and the T15 page still lists only TIP-1166, so there is no lock to diff and no timestamp to simulate; TIP-1094 zone deposit forwarding is not in the published scope.

Tempo publishes aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu binaries and a linux/arm64 image; no source names validator CPUs. On aarch64 evm2 always uses the NEON kernel (no runtime choice). That kernel, compiled from the unchanged source with a software model of its intrinsics, gives the reference JUMPDEST map on all 442,577 bytecodes including the deployed PoolManager, and a planted lookup fault is caught on 300,470. Native aarch64 code generation is left as a low lead.

Yes, ruint 1.21.1 has x86-only code: _subborrow_u64 in the comparison and subtraction chain, and the x86 div instruction in the reciprocal and in single-limb division. mul_mod, add_mod and the 2^256-1 fast path call these but have no target code of their own. The x86 build and a build forced onto the non-x86 branches both match num-bigint on 30 million iterations of all U256 operations evm2 uses, with 7.5 million cases in the 1.21.0 fault shape, on which 1.21.0 fails 2,834,980 times. Tempo publishes aarch64 builds; whether a validator runs one is not public.
